presets.name: Standard
presets.desc: Every fader at 0 dB: bit-transparent, the starting point to draw a curve from
presets.notes: golem's Standard preset kept as is

presets.name: Bass smiley
presets.desc: +4 dB at 60 Hz and +2 at 2 – 4 kHz around a small 500 Hz dip, the top rolled off: a round, present bass
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is; its top two faders now act at 12 and 16 kHz (GxGraphicEQ's top bands sat higher)

presets.name: Hygiaphone
presets.desc: Everything below 250 Hz and above 8 kHz at -12 dB, a +4 dB bump at 1 – 2 kHz: a voice through a ticket-window grille
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is. The faders hold their values: -12 at 8 kHz is -12 there, not a gentle skirt

presets.name: Lead boost
presets.desc: +3 dB at 1 kHz and +4 at 2 kHz, the 8 kHz fizz down 1 dB: a lead that cuts through without more gain
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is

presets.name: Lo-fi radio
presets.desc: Lows and highs falling away from a +3 dB 500 Hz – 1 kHz hump: a small transistor radio
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is; the top cut starts at 12 kHz here, a little lower and more audible than on GxGraphicEQ

presets.name: Vocal shape
presets.desc: Lows below 125 Hz cut hard, +2 – 3 dB from 4 to 12 kHz: a clear, airy voice above the band
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is

presets.name: V shape
presets.desc: -4 dB at 1 kHz and -3 at 500 Hz between a +2 dB 125 Hz and +3 at 4 kHz: a scooped rhythm
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is

presets.name: Solo lift
presets.desc: Guitar 7: +4 dB at 800 Hz, +3 at 1.6 kHz, +1 at 400 Hz and 3 dB of level: the solo voicing on a footswitch
presets.notes: The classic 7-band trick: a mid lift plus level. Accurate mode means +4 at 800 Hz is +4, with no pile-up between 800 and 1.6k

presets.name: Mid push for fuzz
presets.desc: Guitar 7: +2 dB at 400 Hz, +5 at 800 Hz, +3 at 1.6 kHz: puts back the mids a fuzz scoops out
presets.notes: After a scooped fuzz, so it is heard in a band mix instead of disappearing under the bass and cymbals

presets.name: Tight front end
presets.desc: -15 dB at 30 Hz, -10 at 60 Hz, -4 at 125 Hz, +3 at 1 kHz and +2 at 2 kHz: a tight low end into a high-gain amp
presets.notes: Before the amp: the lows the amp would turn into mush are cut by faders, with no peaking at 125 Hz

presets.name: Scooped rhythm
presets.desc: After the amp: +2 dB at 250 Hz and 8 kHz around -4 to -5 dB at 500 Hz – 1 kHz
presets.notes: Post-amp scoop; for a band mix keep it shallow, the mids are where a guitar is heard

presets.name: Post-cab tame
presets.desc: Low cut 80 Hz, steep high cut 8 kHz and -2 dB at 4 kHz: a cab sim's rumble and fizz removed
presets.notes: The cuts the faders cannot do: a 30 Hz fader at -15 dB is not a high-pass

presets.name: Slap smile
presets.desc: Bass 7: +4 dB at 50 Hz and 10 kHz, +3 at 4.5 kHz, -4 / -3 dB at 400 / 500 Hz: a slap bass scoop
presets.notes: The two low-mid faders a third of an octave apart make one clean dip, with no hole between them

presets.name: Bass growl
presets.desc: Bass 7: +5 dB at 800 Hz, +2 at 120 Hz, -2 at 4.5 kHz: a growling, midrange-forward bass
presets.notes: The 800 Hz push is what lets a bass be heard on small speakers and under distorted guitars

presets.name: Piezo de-quack
presets.desc: Low cut 70 Hz, -4 dB at 1 kHz and -2 at 500 Hz, +2 at 12 kHz: an acoustic's piezo without the quack
presets.notes: The piezo's honk lives around 1 kHz; the 12 kHz lift gives back some of the air a mic would hear

presets.name: Telephone
presets.desc: Low cut 300 Hz, steep high cut 3.4 kHz and +4 dB at 1 kHz: a telephone line
presets.notes: The telephone band is 300 Hz – 3.4 kHz; the cuts do it, the 1 kHz fader adds the honk

presets.name: Bright clean sparkle
presets.desc: +3 dB at 8 kHz, +2 at 12 kHz and -2 at 125 Hz: a clean guitar with more sheen and less boom

presets.name: Dark jazz
presets.desc: -4 dB at 4 kHz down to -8 at 12 kHz, +2 at 125 Hz: a dark, round archtop tone

presets.name: Bedroom to stage
presets.desc: -3 dB at 60 Hz and +2 at 2 kHz: a tone dialled at home that would boom and vanish in a room with a band

shift.name: Shift L
shift.help: Moves every partial by this many Hz (left, and the base of the right)

fbk.name: Feedback
fbk.help: The shifted wet fed back: each pass is shifted again

time.name: Time
time.help: Delay before the shifter, inside the loop

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Linear dry / wet crossfade (the catalogue's law)

shift_r.name: Shift R
shift_r.help: Right shift as a ratio of the left: +100 % = same (phase-locked), 0 = right unshifted, −100 % = opposite (stereo spread)

loop.name: Loop
loop.help: Phaser adds a dispersive 12-stage all-pass chain in the loop: a denser barber-pole phaser at time 0 (Delay alone already phases, through the Hilbert pair)

sideband.name: Sideband
sideband.help: +100 = the signed shift only; 0 = both sidebands (carrier-free ring mod); −100 = the mirror (Bode's Up / Down mix)

zero_cut.name: Zero Cut
zero_cut.help: Removes the partials shifted below 0 Hz (no mud) or past Nyquist, by a second pass through the Hilbert pair

dry_match.name: Dry Match
dry_match.help: Dry through the wet's own all-pass path: small shifts swell like a tremolo instead of phasing; shift 0 nulls to −83 dB

time_sync.name: Time Sync
time_sync.help: time from the host tempo (a duration)

low_cut.name: Loop Low Cut
low_cut.help: In the feedback return: each pass thinner

high_cut.name: Loop High Cut
high_cut.help: In the feedback return: each pass darker; tames upward spirals

lfo_depth.name: LFO Depth
lfo_depth.help: ± Hz added to the shift by the LFO; may cross zero

sync.name: LFO Sync
sync.help: LFO period and phase from the host position (shared id)

env_depth.name: Envelope Depth
env_depth.help: Hz added by the input envelope: the pick pushes the shift

presets.name: Endless phase
presets.desc: Every partial moved up 0.3 Hz against the dry: notches that climb for ever and never turn round
presets.notes: The barber-pole phaser with no feedback: the dry beats against the shifted wet; 50 % mix gives the deepest notches

presets.name: Spiral phaser
presets.desc: A dense barber-pole phaser: the shifted wet fed back through a twelve-stage all-pass chain
presets.notes: Costello's recipe: a dispersive loop around the shifter; more feedback, sharper notches

presets.name: Falling flanger
presets.desc: Comb teeth that glide down for ever: a 3 ms loop shifted −0.4 Hz on every pass
presets.notes: A short delay in the loop turns the barber-pole phaser into a flanger; the loop high cut keeps the teeth smooth

presets.name: Wide metallic detune
presets.desc: Left shifted up 1.5 Hz, right down 1.5 Hz, 12 ms late: a sweet metallic chorus that spreads wide
presets.notes: Opposite stereo shifts; summed to mono they are both sidebands, a slow ring-mod shimmer

presets.name: Whole-band swell
presets.desc: The whole chord swells and fades four times a second: the dry matched to the wet's phase
presets.notes: Dry Match puts every partial's beat in phase: a tremolo made of beating, not a phaser

presets.name: Bell lead
presets.desc: Every partial moved up 180 Hz: harmonics turn inharmonic, single notes ring like bells
presets.notes: Inharmonic partials over a dry core; play single notes, chords turn to clang

presets.name: Carrier-free ring mod
presets.desc: Both sidebands at ±400 Hz, no carrier and no dry: a clean ring modulator
presets.notes: Sideband 0 mixes the shift and its mirror at −6 dB each: a sine ring modulator without carrier bleed

presets.name: Through-zero swirl
presets.desc: The shift swings ±3 Hz around zero: the phasing slows, stops and reverses on a slow cycle
presets.notes: The oscillator's phase is continuous, so crossing 0 Hz never steps

presets.name: Pick zap
presets.desc: Each pick attack pushes the shift up to 600 Hz and lets it fall back: a zap on every note
presets.notes: The envelope drives the shift in Hz; play staccato for separate zaps

presets.name: Falling ghost echoes
presets.desc: Echoes 350 ms apart, each one 30 Hz lower and thinner than the last
presets.notes: Zero Cut keeps the falling repeats from folding back into mud below 0 Hz

presets.name: Rising spiral echoes
presets.desc: Quarter-second echoes that climb 12 Hz per repeat and darken as they go
presets.notes: A shifter in a delay loop; Zero Cut also removes what climbs past Nyquist

presets.name: Runaway wall
presets.desc: Feedback past 100 %: the loop builds into a bounded, ever-rising wall; lower it to recover
presets.notes: Meant for an EXP pedal on Feedback; the soft clip on the return keeps it bounded

presets.name: Bass growl
presets.desc: Bass shifted 60 Hz down with the zero cut off: low notes fold back through 0 Hz and growl
presets.notes: The through-zero reflection on purpose; mixed low so the fundamental stays

presets.name: Radio ghost
presets.desc: A 24 Hz shift with a short, faint loop and a nearly dry right side: a voice between stations
presets.notes: The catalogue's radio-ghost converted to real units (README §3.4)

presets.name: Metal smear
presets.desc: Partials moved up 40 Hz on the left, 16 Hz on the right, smeared by a 15 ms loop
presets.notes: The catalogue's metal-smear converted to real units (README §3.4)

presets.name: Barber pole
presets.desc: A 4 Hz shift in a 144 ms loop: echoes that each beat faster, a slow spinning pole
presets.notes: The catalogue's barberpole in real units, with Shift R at +100 % (R = L) as its author meant

rise.name: Rise
rise.help: Swell time from start to full level (when sync = Off)

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Rise as a note value at the host tempo

sens.name: Sensitivity
sens.help: Pick threshold (rise 12 → 3 dB) and the window below the playing level that may trigger (18 → 48 dB)

legato.name: Legato
legato.help: Sensitivity of the pickless detectors (shape flux, pitch jump); 0 = picks only (and cheaper)

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: How far below unity a swell starts: 100 % = from silence, 50 % = attack softened by 6 dB

dip.name: Retrigger Dip
dip.help: How far a new note pulls a ringing note down before swelling; 0 = swell only after silence

strum.name: Strum Window
strum.help: Onsets this close to the first one merge into one swell (strums, slides); also the fastest retrigger

decay.name: Decay (Bow)
decay.help: After the rise, fall back to the start level: attack-decay bows, reverse-tape

reset.name: Reset
reset.help: The swell resets (gain back to the start) once the note has decayed this far below its body level; falling under thresh always resets

release.name: Reset Fade
release.help: Fade to the start level on reset

thresh.name: Noise Floor
thresh.help: Absolute floor: nothing below it triggers or holds a note (hiss, hum)

source.name: Detector Source
source.help: Key = the auxiliary input (the clean DI when the swell sits after the amp)

lookahead.name: Lookahead
lookahead.help: Delays the audio, reported to the host: perfect removal of retriggered attacks

fire.name: Fire
fire.help: Each off → on edge starts a swell (footswitch)

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: The VST3 bypass parameter (make_bypass): golem switches the block with it, so engaging is seen

presets.name: Violin
presets.desc: Each picked note fades in from silence over a quarter second; stop each note before the next
presets.notes: Stopping each note lets the swell reset, so the next pick meets a closed gain: the attack is removed at zero latency

presets.name: Violin after the amp
presets.desc: The violin swell placed after the drive or amp, listening to the clean DI on the key input
presets.notes: Detection on the clean DI: a distorted signal has few transients left and lifts the hiss; needs the DI routed to the key bus

presets.name: Cello pad
presets.desc: Strummed chords swell in slowly as one bowed pad, one swell per strum; best into a long reverb
presets.notes: An 80 ms strum window merges slow strums into one swell; the S-curve lands softly

presets.name: Legato lead
presets.desc: Hammer-ons, pull-offs and slides swell too, not only picked notes; a slide swells once
presets.notes: The pitch-jump detector answers 8 – 16 ms after a legato note: a short blip, then the swell; lookahead 25 ms removes it in the studio

presets.name: Gentle bow changes
presets.desc: A new note only pulls the ringing one down a little before swelling: smooth bow changes
presets.notes: Dip 35 % keeps two thirds of the ringing note under the new one

presets.name: Reverse tape
presets.desc: Every note rises over a quarter note and stops dead: a backwards-tape feel locked to the tempo
presets.notes: Long rise, 40 ms decay: the attack-decay bow of the reverse-tape pedals

presets.name: Bowed stabs
presets.desc: Each note swells in fast and fades away by itself: a bowed attack and decay per note
presets.notes: With a decay the swell is spent after each bow; only a new pick, legato note or fire starts another

presets.name: Tempo swells
presets.desc: Swells that take a half note at the song's tempo, with a pedal-like taper; feed a dotted delay and a long reverb
presets.notes: The swell starts at the note, not on the grid; only its length follows the tempo

presets.name: Soft attack
presets.desc: Takes the edge off each pick: a 25 ms linear fade from half level, nothing else changes
presets.notes: Depth 50 % starts each note 6 dB down: a transient softener rather than a swell

presets.name: Foot swell
presets.desc: Swells only when the footswitch fires: re-swell a held chord on demand
presets.notes: Map Fire to a momentary footswitch; sens 0 and legato 0 leave the picks and legato detectors at their least eager

presets.name: Live clean retriggers
presets.desc: The violin swell with 3 ms of lookahead: re-picked notes lose their attack completely
presets.notes: 3 ms of reported latency hides every pick's dip; set at insert, never switched inside a song

presets.name: Studio perfect swell
presets.desc: The violin swell with 25 ms of lookahead: picked and legato notes all start at silence
presets.notes: For recording and re-amping: 25 ms of reported latency places the legato dips too, down to about 145 Hz

presets.name: Bowed bass
presets.desc: Bass notes fade in like a bowed double bass, at any playing level
presets.notes: Pitch jumps are read above 75 Hz only (from the D string's first frets up); below, legato swells through the flux detector or not at all

presets.name: Pads and keys
presets.desc: Removes the attack of keys and pads: each new chord swells in, even without a transient
presets.notes: The level gate opens after each silence; the flux detector catches a new chord over a ringing one

quant.name: Quant
quant.help: Word size of the virtual converter; fractional for Linear (a sweep has no steps)

rate.name: Rate
rate.help: The virtual clock; 48,000 (or R ≥ fs) = Off

nonlin.name: Non-Lin
nonlin.help: The DAC's power-law curve (thickening), level-neutral at −18 dBFS

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Dry ↔ wet linear crossfade (parallel crush)

law.name: Format
law.help: Word format: uniform, companded or gain-ranging words

quantizer.name: Quantizer
quantizer.help: Where zero sits: silence stays silent / buzzes / dead zone (MDA)

dither.name: Dither
dither.help: TPDF, 100 % = ±1 LSB; tails fade it too

tails.name: Tails
tails.help: Below 1 – 2 LSB: unquantised tail / silence / as is

input.name: Input
input.help: Drive into the converter (clip, use of bits); output compensated

asym.name: Asymmetry
asym.help: Share of nonlin applied to one polarity only (even harmonics)

ladder.name: DAC Error
ladder.help: R-2R bit-weight mismatch: grit on quiet signals (Linear, Float)

rate_shift.name: Rate Shift
rate_shift.help: Transposes the clock down (R = rate · 2^(st / 12)): the EXP sweep control, pitch-like feel

jitter.name: Jitter
jitter.help: Clock jitter, ±25 % of a period at 100 % (seeded)

track.name: Track
track.help: Rate locked to N × the played pitch: aliases on the harmonic series (best at R ≤ 8 kHz)

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Locks the rate LFO to the host tempo (Off: Mod Rate sets it)

env_sens.name: Envelope Sensitivity
env_sens.help: How strongly the playing level drives the rate modulation

env_att.name: Envelope Attack
env_att.help: How fast the envelope follows a rising level

env_rel.name: Envelope Release
env_rel.help: How fast the envelope falls back after a note

presets.name: 8-bit lead
presets.desc: Classic crush: 8-bit words at 16 kHz, aliasing kept, quiet tails faded to clean instead of fizzing
presets.notes: The default: heard at once on insert. Tails Clean keeps a gain stage after it from turning the sputter into fizz

presets.name: Rack sampler 12-bit
presets.desc: Warm 12-bit grit at 26 kHz through steep anti-alias and reconstruction filters
presets.notes: The rack sampler's warmth is its filters, not its bits: 6th-order Butterworth either side of the converter

presets.name: Sampled guitar 12-bit
presets.desc: Clean guitar through a 12-bit sampler at 26 kHz: softened top, grainy tails
presets.notes: Rack Sampler 12 for a clean guitar part played as if sampled from a record

presets.name: Hot-sampled 26k
presets.desc: Drum-machine 12-bit at 26 kHz, sampled with no input filter: ringing aliases, softened images
presets.notes: Aliasing kept on purpose, a 4-pole ladder on the output: the drum-machine voicing [to tune by ear]

presets.name: Companded 8-bit
presets.desc: µ-law 8-bit words at 28 kHz: grain on loud notes, clean quiet tails, no fizz
presets.notes: Eight bits through a µ-law DAC: about 12 bits of dynamic range, the 80s drum machines' trick

presets.name: Phone line
presets.desc: Telephone voice: µ-law 8-bit at 8 kHz, band-limited 300 – 3,400 Hz
presets.notes: G.711's word and band; Clean decimation so nothing folds back into the voice

presets.name: AM radio
presets.desc: Narrow, slightly thickened voice: µ-law 8-bit at 11 kHz, 300 – 4,500 Hz
presets.notes: The old catalogue "AM radio" by intent: band-limited, a touch of DAC curve for density

presets.name: 1-bit fuzz
presets.desc: A one-bit square of the input, gated cleanly as the note decays
presets.notes: Riser at 1 bit is a square whatever the level; input +24 dB sets where the gate closes (about −18 dBFS of DI)

presets.name: Tuned crush
presets.desc: Rate locked to a multiple of the played note: the aliases land on its harmonics, in tune
presets.notes: Monophonic lines: chords hold the last rate. Best at R ≤ 8 kHz where the pitch error beats slowly

presets.name: Tuned arpeggio
presets.desc: Pitch-locked crush stepped through harmonic multiples by an eighth-note LFO
presets.notes: The LFO moves the target rate; track rounds it to whole multiples of f0: an arpeggio of crushes

presets.name: Sample-rate sweep
presets.desc: Expression-pedal sweep of the clock from 48 kHz down to 750 Hz: a glide, no zipper
presets.notes: Assign EXP to rate_shift (0 → −72 st): pitch-like travel, the fractional clock glides between every rate

presets.name: Pick-harder crush
presets.desc: The rate drops as the attack rises: harder picking crunches more
presets.notes: Envelope on the clock, negative depth: dynamics play the crush

presets.name: Synced wobble
presets.desc: Clock swept by an eighth-note sine around 8 kHz, locked to the tempo
presets.notes: Deterministic and host-synced: the same wobble on every take

presets.name: Dusty jitter
presets.desc: 10-bit sampler at 12 kHz with a wandering clock: aliases smeared into dust
presets.notes: Clock jitter turns the images and aliases into noise while the pitch stays put

presets.name: Parallel grit
presets.desc: Six-bit crush at 6 kHz blended under the dry: grit on top, the low end kept
presets.notes: The dry runs through the kernels' own response: no comb in the blend below the rate

presets.name: Old ladder DAC
presets.desc: 12-bit sampler whose ladder DAC mis-steps at mid-scale: crossover grit on quiet notes
presets.notes: R-2R bit-weight errors: quiet signals cross the wrong-sized mid-scale step [magnitude to tune by ear]

presets.name: Hit the converter
presets.desc: Input pushed 12 dB into a 10-bit converter: hard digital clipping, level compensated
presets.notes: Rate Off: the clip runs at the host rate, as a real overloaded ADC

presets.name: Clean decimate
presets.desc: Bandwidth only: 16-bit at 8 kHz through elliptic filters, no foldover
presets.notes: A brick-wall "small speaker": the Clean model removes every alias

pitch.name: Pitch
pitch.help: Carrier = base × this interval (−60 … +60 st), Free and Track: the musical carrier sweep

ring.name: Ring Mod
ring.help: 1 = pure ring modulation; lower blends the carrier as a sine voice

feedback.name: Feedback
feedback.help: mda's recursive ring: the output fed back into the multiplier, cascaded sidebands

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Linear crossfade dry ↔ wet (catalogue law)

thr.name: Threshold
thr.help: Under this level the tracker holds its note and the wet is squelched (0 = never)

speed.name: Speed
speed.help: Carrier glide between notes (Surge's law, 208 → 24 ms)

lowcut.name: Low Cut
lowcut.help: Detector high-pass (detection only); also sets the lowest tracked note (÷ 1.75)

model.name: Model
model.help: Ideal multiplier or Parker diode ring (Ring mode)

tuning.name: Tuning
tuning.help: Just ratios make tracked intervals beat-free

lock.name: Phase Lock
lock.help: Track: carrier phase-locked to the fundamental (the loop engages and releases by itself, without a step)

snap.name: Snap
snap.help: Track: new notes jump instead of gliding

phase.name: Lock Phase
phase.help: Track + lock, at unison, octaves and half ratios: which harmonics add or cancel

drive.name: Drive
drive.help: Input saturation, 0 – 24 dB into tanh (Clean); input into the ring (Diode)

carrier_level.name: Carrier Level
carrier_level.help: Diode: starved and gated ↔ hard switching

shape.name: LFO Shape
shape.help: Square = trill between two carriers; Random = seeded S&H, slewed 2 ms

env_sens.name: Env Sensitivity
env_sens.help: How loud the playing must be to move the envelope

env_rel.name: Env Release
env_rel.help: How fast the envelope falls back

presets.name: Ring standard
presets.desc: The input times a 450 Hz sine: bell-like sum and difference tones, 100 % wet
presets.notes: Re-authored: the catalogue's 0.3 was 4.85 kHz, a whistle on a guitar; 450 Hz is a musical ring

presets.name: Bell tone
presets.desc: A 1 kHz sine carrier: struck-metal partials over every note
presets.notes: Re-authored from 8.86 kHz (a whistle) to about 1 kHz

presets.name: Robot voice
presets.desc: A 39 Hz carrier with mda feedback: the classic metallic robot voice
presets.notes: Re-authored from 1.95 kHz: robot voices sit at 30 to 50 Hz; the wet low cut keeps the difference tones clean

presets.name: Ring solo
presets.desc: A 530 Hz ring blended under the dry, sum tones tamed by a 6 kHz wet high cut
presets.notes: Dry at 30 % keeps the played pitch audible

presets.name: Bell tower
presets.desc: Diode ring at 1 kHz, carrier driven past the knee: square-like sidebands, gong-like arpeggios
presets.notes: The diodes switch at +3 dB: odd carrier harmonics add sidebands

presets.name: Transmitter
presets.desc: An 80 Hz diode ring band-limited to 300 Hz – 3.5 kHz: a voice through a radio link
presets.notes: fine 0.8 = 80 Hz with freq at 0

presets.name: Tremolo to clang
presets.desc: A 6 Hz carrier at half mix is a true tremolo; sweep Pitch up and it turns into ring clangour
presets.notes: Put the expression pedal on pitch 0.5 → 0.9 (6 → 96 Hz)

presets.name: Slow sweep
presets.desc: A 320 Hz carrier swept ±12 semitones by a 0.3 Hz LFO: sidebands that glide through the note
presets.notes: The analog ring pedal's LFO move

presets.name: Broken radio
presets.desc: Mismatched diodes on a starved carrier: the carrier leaks and the ring gates, under a 3 kHz cut
presets.notes: thr 0 keeps the leak audible in the gaps

presets.name: Ring tracker
presets.desc: A carrier that follows the note at unison, half ring half sine voice, half mix
presets.notes: The catalogue preset's values

presets.name: Octave monster
presets.desc: Tracked carrier an octave up, mostly ring: an octave-up synth voice that glides
presets.notes: The catalogue preset's values (glide τ 87 ms)

presets.name: Sub growl
presets.desc: Tracked carrier an octave down from a bass: hollow sub tones under the note
presets.notes: The catalogue preset's values; lowcut 0.2 lowers the tracked range to 35 Hz

presets.name: Harmonic ring
presets.desc: Phase-locked unison carrier: octave and harmonics of the note, in tune everywhere, no warble
presets.notes: lock keeps the carrier on the string's own frequency

presets.name: Octave synth
presets.desc: Octave-up tracked ring with snap: notes start in tune, the lock removes the tracker's beat
presets.notes: Octave monster without the portamento

presets.name: Hollow sub
presets.desc: Carrier an octave below the note: odd harmonics of f0 / 2, a square-ish sub voice
presets.notes: r = 1/2: the products are harmonics of half the note

presets.name: Fifth organ
presets.desc: A just fifth above the note (3/2): products on harmonics of f0 / 2, an organ-like stack
presets.notes: Just tuning makes the fifth beat-free

presets.name: Glide lead
presets.desc: Mostly sine voice from the tracker with a 200 ms portamento: a mono synth lead
presets.notes: speed 0.3 ≈ 196 ms of glide

presets.name: Sub shift
presets.desc: Lower sideband only, by half the note: a clean shift down that follows what you play
presets.notes: Single sideband: no upper product

gain.name: Drive
gain.help: Gain into the model's stages, linear in dB over the model's own range; loudness-compensated

mix.name: Blend
mix.help: Law: linear crossfade, 0 = clean only, 100 = dirt only; phase-coherent

model.name: Model
model.help: Modern: CMOS grind; Classic: tube-emulation DI push; Vintage: valve-preamp grit

cab.name: Cab
cab.help: Speaker emulation; Off for an amp, a cab or an IR after it

grunt.name: Grunt
grunt.help: Lows into the clipper (pre-clip low shelf at 4 × low_note), added to the model's own

attack.name: Attack
attack.help: Treble into the clipper (pre-clip high shelf at 1.5 kHz), added to the model's own

dirt_level.name: Dirt Level
dirt_level.help: The dirt's level relative to the compensated level (the hardware Level knob)

lo_mid_freq.name: Lo Mid Freq
lo_mid_freq.help: Centre of the Lo Mid band (the hardware positions: 250, 500, 1,000 Hz)

hi_mid_freq.name: Hi Mid Freq
hi_mid_freq.help: Centre of the Hi Mid band, the growl (the hardware positions: 750, 1,500, 3,000 Hz)

bass_keep.name: Bass Keep
bass_keep.help: Below this frequency the bass stays clean, mono and out of the clipper (0 = off)

low_note.name: Lowest Note
low_note.help: The lowest open string: golem sets it from the lane's tuning; every low corner follows it

comp_path.name: Comp Path
comp_path.help: Dirt: compress the driven path only; Both: compress before the clean / dirt split

sag.name: Sag
sag.help: 50 % = the model's own sag; 0 = none, 100 % = double (no effect in Modern)

input.name: Input
input.help: Instrument level into the box (active / passive); not compensated

cab_lows.name: Cab Lows
cab_lows.help: Off: the speaker emulation acts only above the bass

presets.name: Studio DI
presets.desc: A clean DI that sounds miked: a touch of tube push, the smooth speaker emulation, flat EQ
presets.notes: The SansAmp-style use: Blend full, Drive low; the cab's smoothing does most of the work. Turn cab Off before an IR

presets.name: Warm Push
presets.desc: Power-stage push that blooms when dug in, rounded top, the clean under it for the low end
presets.notes: Sag above half lets the power stage sag more on hard notes

presets.name: Modern Grind
presets.desc: CMOS-style grind blended over a full clean, growl boosted at 1.5 kHz, low mids scooped
presets.notes: The coherent blend keeps the clean lows at full weight under the grind; Hi Mid at 1.5 kHz is the growl

presets.name: Tight Five
presets.desc: Grind for 5- and 6-strings: lows below 110 Hz kept clean, mono and out of the cab
presets.notes: low_note comes from the lane's tuning; Grunt −6 and Bass Keep keep the low B out of the clipper

presets.name: Drop Growl
presets.desc: Drop-tuned growl: heavy grind with the hi-mid bark, clean low end held under 90 Hz
presets.notes: Bass Keep is the guarantee that the fundamental of a drop-A string never thins in the blend

presets.name: Valve Grit
presets.desc: Low-gain valve grind with the mids forward and a darker top, through a sealed 8×10
presets.notes: Sag at its default moves the bias with the playing: the grind blooms when dug in

presets.name: Ultra Scoop
presets.desc: Scooped valve DI: −10 dB at 500 Hz, a little more bass and top, light grit
presets.notes: The valve DI's 'ultra low' switch as a preset: the Lo Mid cut at 500 Hz does it

presets.name: Slap Even
presets.desc: Compressor before everything evens slap and pop; a hint of grit, bass and treble up, mids cut
presets.notes: Comp Path Both: the clean is compressed too, so the thumb and the pop come out level

presets.name: Engine Grind
presets.desc: Compressed grind blended with an uncompressed clean: an even dirt, the dynamics kept underneath
presets.notes: The compressor sits in the dirt only (the amp-head engine's way): the clean keeps every accent

presets.name: Fuzz Wall Low
presets.desc: Full-gain grind with the treble pushed into the clipper: a synth-like fuzz wall over the clean
presets.notes: 8× oversampling and the interstage low-pass keep the aliases about 100 dB under the note at full gain

presets.name: Into the IR
presets.desc: Modern grind with the speaker emulation off, for a cab IR block after it
presets.notes: Cab Off: the IR (golem's cab block) does the speaker; golem writes Off when a cab follows

presets.name: Grit Blend Pedal
presets.desc: Clean to grit on the expression pedal: the blend sweeps without thinning, the lows never move
presets.notes: Put Blend on the EXP pedal (0 → 70 %); Bass Keep 100 Hz keeps the fundamental clean at every point

presets.name: Guitar DI
presets.desc: The tube-emulation DI on guitar: corners scaled to the guitar's low E, smooth speaker
presets.notes: golem sets low_note to 82.4 Hz on a guitar lane: every low corner moves up an octave with it

input.name: Record
input.help: How hard the tape is hit: 0 dB puts a -18 dBFS note at the machine's reference; the output stays level

wow.name: Wow
wow.help: Peak slow speed deviation (% of speed); the model sets its spectrum

flutter.name: Flutter
flutter.help: Peak fast speed deviation (% of speed), 4 - 200 Hz

wear.name: Wear
wear.help: Age and failures in the model's own way: dull heads, dropouts, crinkles, snags or crackle

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Dry ↔ wet crossfade, dry aligned (50 % + wow = tape chorus)

speed.name: Speed
speed.help: Tape speed: losses, bump, EQ, transport scale; inert on Vinyl / Shellac / Radio

bias.name: Bias
bias.help: Under 100 %: crossover grit and a brighter top; over: cleaner and darker

head_bump.name: Head Bump
head_bump.help: Contour effect, relative to the model's

spacing.name: Spacing
spacing.help: Head-to-tape gap: highs vanish first, much more at low speed

azimuth.name: Azimuth
azimuth.help: Head tilt in arc-minutes: duller highs; in stereo a delay between the tracks

wow_rate.name: Wow Speed
wow_rate.help: Scales the speed of every slow wobble of the transport

wow_rand.name: Wow Randomness
wow_rand.help: Negative: a regular, machine-like wobble; positive: erratic

drop_sync.name: Dropout Sync
drop_sync.help: Puts the dropouts on the host grid (Off: random)

noise_mode.name: Noise Mode
noise_mode.help: Follow: noise only under the playing; Constant: always; Duck: in the gaps

mech.name: Mechanical
mech.help: Relative to the model's motor / rumble noise

stop.name: Stop
stop.help: Tape stop: the motor winds down; off spins it back up

stop_time.name: Stop Time
stop_time.help: Stop ramp; spin-up = ¼ of it

spread.name: Spread
spread.help: Stereo: the random wobble and failures differ left and right

presets.name: Studio glue
presets.desc: 15 ips reel hit 6 dB hot: soft compression and a rounder top, transport inaudible, no hiss
presets.notes: The always-on setting: hysteresis at 100 % bias glues without fuzz (about 1 % THD on a -18 dBFS note)

presets.name: Hot 30 sheen
presets.desc: 30 ips mastering reel driven 9 dB: tight lows under a 76 Hz bump, highs barely compressed
presets.notes: At 30 ips the record boost is only 1.5 dB at 10 kHz: the tape compresses the body, not the air

presets.name: Bass bump
presets.desc: 15 ips reel with its 38 Hz head bump under the fundamental and a slightly over-biased, rounder attack

presets.name: Under-biased grit
presets.desc: Home reel at 7½ ips, under-biased and hit hard: crossover grit on quiet notes, a dirty clean
presets.notes: Bias 60 % opens the loop: quiet notes lose level and gain grit, as a mis-aligned machine does

presets.name: Cassette demo
presets.desc: Type I cassette with a compander: highs saturate first, the noise reduction breathes with the playing

presets.name: Four-track double speed
presets.desc: Cassette at 3¾ ips through the compander, driven 10 dB: the portastudio's bounce

presets.name: Personal player warble
presets.desc: Portable cassette with random wow, automatic level control and worn tape: lo-fi chords

presets.name: Melted tape
presets.desc: Cassette whose wow is meant for the expression pedal: 0.2 % at heel, toe to 4 % for melting pitch
presets.notes: Map EXP to wow 0.2 - 4 %: the read head's centre rises at 20 ms/s, so the sweep sags in pitch like a slowing tape

presets.name: VHS chorus
presets.desc: VHS linear track half wet against the aligned dry: a centred warble chorus, widened by spread

presets.name: Dictaphone voice
presets.desc: Microcassette band (300 Hz - 5 kHz), automatic level pumping and motor noise on a voice

presets.name: Dusty vinyl keys
presets.desc: Worn LP: crackle and scratches in the gaps, out of the way while the chords play
presets.notes: Duck keeps the crackle in the gaps; scratches repeat every 1.8 s, one rotation

presets.name: Shellac 78
presets.desc: 78 rpm shellac: 100 Hz - 5 kHz, heavy tracing and loud surface noise, always on

presets.name: Dropout rhythm
presets.desc: Cassette dropouts locked to eighth notes: the highs gate in time, like tape losing contact

presets.name: Tape stop stomp
presets.desc: Studio reel with the stop on a footswitch: 800 ms wind-down to silence and a spin-up back in
presets.notes: Assign Stop to a footswitch; the input during the stop is not recorded, as on a real machine

presets.name: Seasick lead
presets.desc: Home reel with a strong, regular, machine-like wobble: periodic wow at 1.2 %

presets.name: Crumbling archive
presets.desc: Old home-reel tape: dropouts, crinkles, snags and a tilted head that dulls the mono sum

presets.name: Drum bus tape
presets.desc: 15 ips reel driven 12 dB on the drums: softened transients and compressed cymbals, no hiss

presets.name: Parallel tape drive
presets.desc: Cassette slammed 18 dB, blended at 40 % with the aligned dry: thick low-mids, no comb

presets.name: Dirty heads
presets.desc: Home reel with 4 µm of head spacing, meant for the expression pedal: a speed-dependent tone control
presets.notes: Map EXP to spacing 0 - 10 µm: the highs fold away first, as dirt on a head does

presets.name: Grit
presets.desc: A sampled bite on the high mids of drums and loops, lows and highs untouched
presets.notes: golem's catalogue default, converted faithfully: a 7.6 kHz hold then +7.2 dB on the 1.5 – 2.5 kHz band

presets.name: Megaphone
presets.desc: Lows and highs pulled down, hard clip in the low mids, a heavy curve and a 1.26 kHz peak above
presets.notes: golem's catalogue preset, converted; its Peak now sounds (+9 dB at 1.26 kHz), inert in the headless Prisma

presets.name: Telephone
presets.desc: Outer bands muted into a 300 Hz – 3.3 kHz band-pass, light crunch and crushed bits inside
presets.notes: golem's catalogue preset, converted: Soft clip 16 dB, 7.6 bits, a 14 kHz hold; −60 dB is a mute

presets.name: Broken
presets.desc: Fold on the low mids, crushed and ring-modulated high mids, a sampled top, 80 % wet
presets.notes: golem's catalogue preset, converted: Fold 19.6 dB, 6.1 bits, ring at 159 Hz, a 2.5 kHz hold on the top

presets.name: Bass Split
presets.desc: Fundamental clean below 250 Hz, tube grind on the low mids, hard clip above it rolled off at 4 kHz
presets.notes: The clean-low, dirty-mids bass move with crossovers instead of a parallel blend; LR8 keeps the lows out of the clip

presets.name: Bass Growl Parallel
presets.desc: Bass Split with each driven band blended back with its own clean: growl without losing the pick
presets.notes: The per-band blend has no comb: the dry is aligned with the driven path

presets.name: Chord Clarity
presets.desc: Soft clip on four bands: high-gain rhythm chords that keep their notes apart
presets.notes: Notes in different bands do not intermodulate (Anderton's multiband point); into a clean amp. EXP on focus sweeps body to fizz

presets.name: Tight Low Drive
presets.desc: Clean lows under a hot mid band, a light clipped top rolled off at 6 kHz, for drop-tuned riffs
presets.notes: The 'tight' boost done with bands: nothing below 160 Hz reaches a clipper

presets.name: No-Fizz Lead
presets.desc: Tube and soft clip on the mids, the band above 2.5 kHz left clean and 6 dB down
presets.notes: Dirt without fizz: the top band never meets a shaper

presets.name: Drum Bus Crunch
presets.desc: Parallel crunch on a drum bus: heavy low mids, soft-clipped high mids, crushed top, kick untouched
presets.notes: All three are memoryless, so the 60 % blend has no notch; the low band stays clean

presets.name: Tight Kick
presets.desc: A dead zone on the kick's band only: the hit passes, the tail falls into it
presets.notes: Prisma's own two-module idea folded into two slots: dead zone −27 dBFS, +2.4 dB after; to set by ear on the bench

presets.name: Fold Synth Top
presets.desc: Sine fold on the high mids, triangle fold on the top rolled off at 6 kHz, a clean body
presets.notes: Quality on (4×): folders are the widest-band modules

presets.name: Radio Air
presets.desc: A band-limited, sampled voice: a 5 kHz hold on the high mids, no top, thin lows
presets.notes: Lighter than Telephone: the low mids stay clean

presets.name: Fuzz Upper
presets.desc: Fuzz on the low and high mids only: a solo fuzz whose low band never gates or farts out
presets.notes: Fuzz without mud: the lows below 112 Hz pass clean

presets.name: Edge to Wreck
presets.desc: Light crunch on every band, built for an EXP pedal on Drive: one sweep takes it to a wreck
presets.notes: Drive adds up to +24 dB on each saturator, each along its own law; the make-up keeps the level near

gain.name: Gain
gain.help: The circuit's gain pot, by rotation, with its real taper (Blend OD: both gangs, so the clean fades as the gain rises)

tone_stack.name: Tone
tone_stack.help: The circuit's tone pot by rotation, 0 % = darkest on every circuit

level.name: Level
level.help: Output; 0 dB = unity loudness at the defaults on every circuit

diodes.name: Clippers
diodes.help: Swaps the clipping devices in place (the classic mods)

opamp.name: Op-Amp
opamp.help: The macromodel of the circuit's gain-stage op-amp(s); linear stamps and followers are not touched

supply.name: Supply
supply.help: Relative to the circuit's own supply (9 V; the Blend OD's pumped rails follow; the Discrete OD's 8.1 V through its regulator): headroom, bias, rails

hp.name: HP Mode
hp.help: MOSFET OD's HP / LP switch (22 kΩ across the 33 kΩ: louder, brighter); inert on the other circuits

tight.name: Tight
tight.help: Shared id: first-order high-pass at the circuit's input, on top of its own filters; bypassed at 20 Hz

input.name: Input
input.help: Input trim, for a source hotter or weaker than a pickup at 0 dBFS = 1 V

bass_keep.name: Bass Keep
bass_keep.help: Shared id: below it the signal skips the clipping

fat.name: Fat
fat.help: Discrete OD's bass switch (the "Custom" variant: 83 nF switched across the 18 nF into the tone pot = the 101 nF "Phat" position): +5 dB at 120 Hz, +8 dB at 40…

contour.name: Contour
contour.help: Plexi Dist's Contour pot (50 kΩ log rheostat in its bridged T), by rotation: 0 % = deepest mid scoop (−11.7 dB at 1 kHz re 100 Hz), 50 % −7.2 dB, 70 % −4.6 dB,…

presets.name: Slew wall
presets.desc: Slow op-amp hard clipper at 70 %: a thick, compressed rhythm wall without fizz

refs.why: op-amp distortion pedal rhythm tones of the early 90s

presets.notes: The LM308's slew and narrow closed loop round the clip before the diodes: thick, not fizzy. Into a clean amp

presets.name: Filter lead
presets.desc: High gain with the filter just under noon: a vocal, focused op-amp lead
presets.notes: The filter does the voicing: 45 % puts its corner near 3.5 kHz

presets.name: Open op-amp crunch
presets.desc: Low gain, filter open: the op-amp barely slews, an open crunch into a clean amp
presets.notes: Below 40 % gain the closed loop stays wide: a crunch that cleans up with the guitar's volume

presets.name: LED clip
presets.desc: LED clippers in the op-amp circuit: louder, more open, the rail clipping heard
presets.notes: The classic LED mod: the clip at 1.6 V lets the op-amp's rails shape the top

presets.name: Op-amp only
presets.desc: Diodes lifted: the rail clipping and slew of the raw LM308
presets.notes: No clipper: the op-amp's own rails and slew are the whole distortion, raw and loud

presets.name: Dying battery
presets.desc: Supply at 70 %: lower rails and bias, a sputtering, gated decay
presets.notes: A tired battery: less headroom and an earlier, uneven breakup as notes decay

presets.name: Op-amp bass drive
presets.desc: Op-amp distortion over a clean fundamental (below 120 Hz kept out of the clip)
presets.notes: bass_keep sends the low band through the filter and output stage only: grit on top, the low end clean

presets.name: Booster crunch into a stack
presets.desc: Transistor booster, op-amp and diodes with the mid scoop, into a cranked amp
presets.notes: Thin into a clean amp, right into a pushed one: tight 120 Hz keeps the lows from flubbing

presets.name: Booster lead
presets.desc: The booster soft-clipping ahead of the diodes: a singing, sustaining lead
presets.notes: The common-emitter booster clips softly ahead of the op-amp: sustain without fizz

presets.name: Transparent push
presets.desc: Low gain, the clean feeds dominant: mids filled in, a clean boost into a pushed amp
presets.notes: The sum on the pumped rails never clips: the guitar's own tone with more push

presets.name: Gritty core
presets.desc: Germanium grit and a 9 V gain stage over a clean core, the sum phase-coherent by circuit
presets.notes: The clean bass path stays at every gain: grit over a clean low end

presets.name: Blend into drive
presets.desc: Blend overdrive at 15 % as the first of two drives: tightens and pushes the next
presets.notes: Put a second instance on Op-Amp Dist after it: the first fills the mids and pushes the clipper

presets.name: Amp in a box
presets.desc: MOSFET overdrive at 55 %: the body-diode knee into a second gain stage, amp-like
presets.notes: Two op-amp stages with the clip between them: louder and more open than a TS

presets.name: Asymmetric amp box
presets.desc: MOSFET + germanium clip of some units: asymmetric, more even harmonics
presets.notes: The rarer germanium version: 0.6 / 0.9 V clipping, a touch of 2nd harmonic

presets.name: HP roar
presets.desc: MOSFET overdrive in HP mode at 70 %: brighter, looser, louder
presets.notes: HP parallels 22 kΩ on the 33 kΩ output resistor: less loss, more top

presets.name: Germanium op-amp dist
presets.desc: Germanium clippers in the op-amp circuit: a softer knee, more output
presets.notes: 1N34A at about 0.3 V: a softer, compressed clip

presets.name: Edge of breakup
presets.desc: Discrete op-amp stage clipping softly on its rails: cleans up with the guitar's volume

refs.why: discrete blues overdrive at low gain over a clean amp

presets.notes: Tone below noon tames the circuit's famous treble; stage 2 breaks up unevenly, the even order of its class-A output

presets.name: Cranked blues
presets.desc: Both discrete stages pushed: asymmetric breakup with a bass bump, into a clean amp
presets.notes: The diodes after stage 1 and stage 2's rails share the clipping: thick, still touch-sensitive

presets.name: Fat blues
presets.desc: The discrete overdrive with its bass switch on: low-end weight under a mild breakup
presets.notes: Fat switches 83 nF across the 18 nF into the tone pot: about +5 dB at 120 Hz, +2 dB at 1 kHz

presets.name: Volume-knob blues
presets.desc: Even-order discrete breakup that cleans up as the guitar's volume rolls back
presets.notes: The pair and the class-A PNP make the 2nd harmonic before any rail: roll the guitar back for a clean core

presets.name: Studio crunch
presets.desc: Upper-mid pre-emphasis into two clippers, lows tightened: a session-player rhythm crunch
presets.notes: Tight 120 Hz stands in for the clones' Bass knob: the stock bass shelf is huge

presets.name: Spectrum lead
presets.desc: Bright Spectrum over a bass shelf that saturates on low notes: a singing overdrive lead
presets.notes: IC2B clips on its rails on low notes: the low end compresses while the top stays open

presets.name: Dark spectrum
presets.desc: Spectrum turned dark, the 700 Hz roll-off: a warm, articulate edge for clean-ish parts
presets.notes: Low gain keeps the feedback clipper soft; the dark Spectrum takes the fizz off

presets.name: Plexi crunch
presets.desc: Three op-amp gain stages with a bright cap at low gain, mids kept: a cranked-stack rhythm

refs.why: cranked plexi-style rhythm crunch

presets.notes: Into a clean amp; the contour at 70 % keeps the mids forward

presets.name: Scooped stack
presets.desc: The bridged-T scoop fully in at high gain, lows tightened: an 80s metal rhythm
presets.notes: Contour 0 % dips 1 kHz by about 12 dB re 100 Hz

presets.name: Plexi bass
presets.desc: Marshall-in-a-box drive on the upper band, the fundamental kept clean below 100 Hz
presets.notes: Bass keep sends the low band through the post-clipper network made linear (polarity matched)

attack.name: Attack
attack.help: Gain on a full transient; + = more punch, − = softer

sustain.name: Sustain
sustain.help: Gain on the tail once it has decayed; + = longer ring, − = tighter

att_time.name: Attack Length
att_time.help: How long the attack gain lasts

sus_time.name: Sustain Length
sus_time.help: Which notes count as decaying: the reference falls at 8.69 / length dB / s

sens.name: Sensitivity
sens.help: The level jump (attack) or fall under the reference (sustain) that counts as full: D_ref = 22 → 2 dB, above a fixed 1.5 dB dead zone

smooth.name: Smooth
smooth.help: Time the gain takes to move into an attack (and the lookahead ramp)

sc_hpf.name: Sidechain Low Cut
sc_hpf.help: Detector high-pass; also sets W (40 ms up to 60 Hz, 20 ms at 120 Hz, 8 ms from 300 Hz): shorter hold, faster sustain response

thresh.name: Noise Floor
thresh.help: Absolute floor: nothing below is shaped, sustain never lifts toward it

source.name: Detector Source
source.help: Key = auxiliary input (the clean DI after an amp)

lookahead.name: Lookahead
lookahead.help: Reported latency; the gain arrives before the transient

ceiling.name: Ceiling Level
ceiling.help: Maximum output level for ceil_mode Soft / Limit

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Linear crossfade dry / shaped (dry delay-aligned)

delta.name: Delta
delta.help: Outputs only what the shaper adds or removes (wet − dry)

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: VST3 bypass parameter (make_bypass), as the coded effects

presets.name: Snap pick
presets.desc: Lifts the pick click on every note by 8 dB on the highs only; the low strings' fundamentals stay put
presets.notes: A shelf at 1.5 kHz carries the boost: the pick gets louder, the bass of a low E is not pumped

presets.name: Soft pick
presets.desc: Takes 9 dB off each pick attack and lets the note through untouched: a rounder, jazzier touch
presets.notes: Zero latency lets a short tick through at each pick; lookahead 2 ms removes it where latency is acceptable

presets.name: Funk pop
presets.desc: Sharper 16th strums: attacks up 10 dB, muted chops pulled down 8 dB, ringing chords left alone
presets.notes: sus_time 250 ms: chops decay faster than the reference and are cut, sustained chords are not. sc_hpf 120 is safe down to a low B

presets.name: Chug tight
presets.desc: Palm-mute definition into a high-gain amp: each chug's attack up 6 dB, its tail cut 10 dB
presets.notes: Placed before the amp. Drop A: sc_hpf 100 (at or under twice the lowest note). Complements a gate

presets.name: Pick definition after the amp
presets.desc: Restores the pick attack an amp compressed, detecting on the clean DI; peaks held under -1 dBFS
presets.notes: The key input carries the DI: a high-gain signal has few level changes left, its DI has them all

presets.name: Ring out
presets.desc: Clean arpeggios ring longer: tails lifted up to 10 dB, never above their height over the noise floor
presets.notes: A 2 s reference shapes slowly decaying notes; thresh just above the rig's hiss keeps the noise from being lifted

presets.name: Bass click
presets.desc: The bass's finger or pick click up 8 dB on the highs; the fundamental is not modulated
presets.notes: A full-band attack on a low E would reshape its first cycle; the shelf moves the boost to the click

presets.name: Bass thump
presets.desc: More knock on each bass note: the lows boosted 6 dB over two full periods of a low E
presets.notes: att_time 60 ms covers whole cycles of a 41 Hz note, so the boost is a thump, not one louder half-cycle

presets.name: Bass even
presets.desc: Fingerstyle evenness without a threshold: plucks softened 6 dB, held notes lifted up to 6 dB
presets.notes: Acts the same at any playing level: a compressor-like evenness with no threshold to set

presets.name: Drum punch
presets.desc: Drum bus punch: hits up 9 dB, tails tightened 4 dB, the boosted peaks soft-clipped under 0 dBFS
presets.notes: sc_hpf 120 shortens the detector's hold to 20 ms. Accents get more than ghost notes

presets.name: Gated snare
presets.desc: Cuts a snare's tail by up to 24 dB at any hit strength, half of it 60 ms after the hit
presets.notes: A tail shaper, not a gate: no threshold to set. For a hard gate, use the gate block

presets.name: Room dry
presets.desc: Pulls a live voice's room down 8 dB after each phrase, leaves held notes alone, at any singing level
presets.notes: A short reference (58 dB / s): only the room's fall after a phrase is faster than it

presets.name: Consonants
presets.desc: Clearer diction: the consonants' attacks up 5 dB on the highs
presets.notes: Pair it with a de-esser placed after

presets.name: Acoustic body
presets.desc: Less pick and more body on an acoustic guitar: attacks down 4 dB, tails up 6 dB
presets.notes: sus_time 800 ms lifts the ring of strummed chords without touching the pick

presets.name: Studio clean punch
presets.desc: Drum punch with the gain in place before each hit and no peak over 0 dBFS (1 ms latency)
presets.notes: Lookahead 1 ms ramps the gain in before the transient: the first cycle is boosted whole. Not for a song that switches lookahead live

amount.name: Amount
amount.help: Scales every band's slope (down and Lift); 0 = flat; held at 30:1

tilt.name: Tilt
tilt.help: ±12 dB of threshold on the outer bands; + = the lows are held and the highs free, − = the reverse

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Crossfade with the aligned dry (OTT's Depth)

character.name: Character
character.help: gfx-comp's dynamics families, no colour, all bands

lo_thresh.name: Low Threshold
lo_thresh.help: Downward threshold of the low band, RMS-calibrated; Tilt moves it

lo_ratio.name: Low Ratio
lo_ratio.help: Downward ratio of the low band (gfx-comp's meaning); Amount scales its slope

lo_lift_thresh.name: Low Lift Threshold
lo_lift_thresh.help: Below this level Lift works on the low band; held at or under the threshold

lo_lift.name: Low Lift
lo_lift.help: Slope below the Lift threshold: + lifts quiet parts (+75 % = 4:1 upward), − expands (−100 % = 1:2)

lo_attack.name: Low Attack
lo_attack.help: How fast the gain of the low band moves down; scaled by Time

lo_release.name: Low Release
lo_release.help: How fast the gain of the low band moves back up; scaled by Time

lo_gain.name: Low Gain
lo_gain.help: Static level of the low band on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ

lo_sc.name: Low Sidechain
lo_sc.help: What the detector of the low band hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)

lm_thresh.name: Low Mid Threshold
lm_thresh.help: Downward threshold of the low-mid band (Mid), RMS-calibrated; Tilt moves it

lm_ratio.name: Low Mid Ratio
lm_ratio.help: Downward ratio of the low-mid band (Mid) (gfx-comp's meaning); Amount scales its slope

lm_lift_thresh.name: Low Mid Lift Threshold
lm_lift_thresh.help: Below this level Lift works on the low-mid band (Mid); held at or under the threshold

lm_lift.name: Low Mid Lift
lm_lift.help: Slope below the Lift threshold: + lifts quiet parts (+75 % = 4:1 upward), − expands (−100 % = 1:2)

lm_attack.name: Low Mid Attack
lm_attack.help: How fast the gain of the low-mid band (Mid) moves down; scaled by Time

lm_release.name: Low Mid Release
lm_release.help: How fast the gain of the low-mid band (Mid) moves back up; scaled by Time

lm_gain.name: Low Mid Gain
lm_gain.help: Static level of the low-mid band (Mid) on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ

lm_sc.name: Low Mid Sidechain
lm_sc.help: What the detector of the low-mid band (Mid) hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)

hm_thresh.name: High Mid Threshold

hm_ratio.name: High Mid Ratio

hm_lift_thresh.name: High Mid Lift Threshold

hm_lift.name: High Mid Lift

hm_attack.name: High Mid Attack

hm_release.name: High Mid Release

hm_gain.name: High Mid Gain
hm_gain.help: Static level of the high-mid band on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ

hm_sc.name: High Mid Sidechain
hm_sc.help: What the detector of the high-mid band hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)

hi_thresh.name: High Threshold

hi_ratio.name: High Ratio

auto_gain.name: Auto Gain

knee.name: Knee
knee.help: gfx-comp's quadratic knee, every band, both thresholds

guard.name: Noise Guard
guard.help: Nothing at or under it is lifted; a boost never exceeds the level's height above it

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: True bypass to the input (delayed by the latency in Linear), 10 ms crossfade

presets.name: Even clean guitar
presets.desc: Three bands at 2.5:1 from −24 dB: strums sit level, the lows never dull the attack of the highs
presets.notes: The fresh plugin: a gentle 3-band leveller, auto gain on (README §4 default row)

presets.name: Tight chug
presets.desc: Palm-mute boom held under 150 Hz at 4:1, 8 ms attack; the riff's top stays open at 1.5:1
presets.notes: After amp and cab. The low band's detector is ripple-free on a low note: the boom is held without added fuzz

presets.name: Acoustic piezo boom
presets.desc: The 180 – 700 Hz body cut 3:1 only when it blooms, quiet top lifted +50 % below −42 dB
presets.notes: Dynamic-EQ use of a band: the piezo's body resonance is only cut when it booms (README §4)

presets.name: Even bass strings
presets.desc: Lows 4:1 below 100 Hz with slow times, mids 3:1, top 2:1 fast: low peaks no longer squash the mids
presets.notes: FET dynamics, no colour. Negative Tilt leaves the lows more of their dynamics: the answer to 'tighter but less powerful'

presets.name: Slap tamer
presets.desc: The even-bass split with the top at 6:1 from −30 dB, 0.5 ms attack: pops caught, fingers untouched
presets.notes: Only the band above 1.5 kHz reacts fast, so the thumb's low end keeps its weight

presets.name: Low anchor, free top
presets.desc: Only the band under 120 Hz compressed, 6:1 Opto: a steady bottom, mids and top untouched
presets.notes: Mid and High at ratio 1 with Lift off pass at unity: a one-band low compressor that never touches the attack

presets.name: Vocal, levelled
presets.desc: Mud (150 – 600 Hz) and harshness (above 4.5 kHz) held only when they occur, Opto dynamics
presets.notes: Keep gfx-deesser before it for the 's'; this handles the broad regions

presets.name: Vocal presence lift
presets.desc: The levelled vocal with 600 Hz – 4.5 kHz lifted +67 % below −40 dB; breaths and room stay down
presets.notes: Quiet syllables come forward; the guard at −66 dBFS keeps the room tone from being lifted

presets.name: Keys bus glue
presets.desc: Three bands at 2:1 from −20 dB, Bus dynamics, slow times; zero latency for live keys
presets.notes: Minimum phase, zero latency: playable live. On a lane that is not played live, phase Linear removes the low-end smear for 42.7 ms of reported latency at 48 kHz

presets.name: Hyper
presets.desc: Every band 30:1 from above and lifted 4:1 from below: the squeezed, detailed sound-design texture
presets.notes: The category's signature, level-matched by auto gain; the guard keeps Lift off the hiss (make-up still lifts it ~10 dB)

presets.name: Hyper, tasteful
presets.desc: The Hyper settings at Amount 40 %: the detail and density without the squash
presets.notes: Amount scales every slope (30:1 becomes about 1.6:1 here), the usual 20 – 40 % way of using it

presets.name: Hyper blend
presets.desc: Full Hyper mixed 30 % under the aligned dry: transients from the dry, density from the wet
presets.notes: Parallel use; the dry is the tree's unity sum, so the blend never combs

presets.name: Pad bloom
presets.desc: Upward only, every band lifted +67 % below −30 dB, slow times: decays and tails bloom evenly
presets.notes: No downward stage (ratio 1): only the quiet parts rise, the guard at −76 dBFS keeps the noise floor down

presets.name: Live vocal de-bleed
presets.desc: Lows and highs expanded 1:2 below −45 dB, 12 dB at most: rumble and cymbals recede between phrases
presets.notes: Downward expansion on the outer bands only: the voice's own region is left alone

presets.name: Lead guitar, even top
presets.desc: Highs above 2.5 kHz 4:1 fast, mids 2:1, quiet tails lifted +40 %: a smooth, singing lead
presets.notes: Negative Tilt eases the low band; Lift in the Mid band carries the sustain without a broadband squash

mode.name: Mode
mode.help: The side generator: Velvet (fine, irregular width), Allpass (no smear, broad colour), Comb (pseudo-stereo), Double (micro-shift), M/S (a stereo source's own width only)

amount.name: Amount
amount.help: Level of the generated side re the mid; 100 % = correlation 0 on a mono source

width.name: Width
width.help: Master side gain (source side and generated); 0 % = mono, 100 % = neutral for a stereo source

time.name: Time
time.help: Velvet length (10 - 40 ms), Comb delay, Double delay; inert in Allpass and M/S

bass_keep.name: Bass Keep
bass_keep.help: Below it the output is mono and dry (a high-pass on the side only); 0 = off

mono_law.name: Mono Law
mono_law.help: Exact: the mono fold is the dry. Classic: true Haas (Comb) and L / R voices (Double); inert elsewhere

variant.name: Variant
variant.help: Which velvet sequence or all-pass set: two lanes on two variants stay distinct

cents.name: Detune
cents.help: Double: each voice is shifted up and down by this much

high_cut.name: Side High Cut
high_cut.help: Low-pass on the generated side only: keeps sibilants and pick noise centred

transient.name: Transient Focus
transient.help: Ducks the generated side on attacks: the pick stays centred, the sustain blooms wide

balance.name: Balance
balance.help: Places the image (positive = right) without touching the mono fold

rotate.name: Rotation
rotate.help: Rotates a stereo image (positive = right); moves the mono fold

listen.name: Listen
listen.help: Audition the mono fold or the side alone (not stored by golem)

presets.name: Wide clean
presets.desc: A mono guitar spread into a fine-grained stereo image; the mono fold is the dry, exactly
presets.notes: The default: correlation about 0.47, each side within ±2 dB in bands; level -1.3 dB matches the bypass in stereo

presets.name: Live safe
presets.desc: Moderate width that survives any PA: exact mono fold at the bypassed level, lows mono, attacks centred
presets.notes: Level stays 0 dB so a mono PA hears the bypass level exactly; one side alone stays within ±2 dB in bands

presets.name: Tight funk
presets.desc: Rhythm parts with the pick centred and punchy and the ring blooming wide behind it
presets.notes: Allpass smears nothing; transient focus ducks the side on each stroke

presets.name: Wall rhythm
presets.desc: Detuned width around a dry centre for high-gain rhythm after the cab; the fold cannot comb
presets.notes: Exact Double: the voices live in the side only, so a mono PA hears the dry riff; high cut keeps the fizz centred

presets.name: Studio double
presets.desc: The classic micro-shift double: two detuned, slightly late voices left and right, heard in mono too
presets.notes: Classic law: the fold carries the double as a chorus; Mono Error shows it

presets.name: Vocal spread
presets.desc: A lead or backing voice widened by detuned voices in the side; sibilants stay centred
presets.notes: High cut 6 kHz keeps esses and breaths in the middle; the fold is the dry voice

presets.name: Air pad
presets.desc: Keys or ambient guitar opened past the speakers: correlation below zero, mono fold still exact
presets.notes: For headphones and recordings rather than a PA: a side louder than the mid reads as outside the speakers

presets.name: Bass sheen
presets.desc: Bass with its lows mono and dry and only the top spread wide
presets.notes: Side-only crossover at 300 Hz: the fundamental never moves; Allpass keeps the attack unsmeared

presets.name: Old pseudo-stereo
presets.desc: The complementary-comb pseudo-stereo of the fifties, exact in mono
presets.notes: Lauridsen's comb: flat in bands but periodic, the classic phasey stereo of reissues

presets.name: Haas pan
presets.desc: A true precedence shift: the right side a few ms late, the image pulled left; combs in mono
presets.notes: Studio, stereo playback only: Mono Error shows the comb the fold takes (notches at 33, 100, 167 Hz)

presets.name: Narrow the keys
presets.desc: A stereo keyboard brought in from the edges, its lows made mono
presets.notes: M/S width only; the mid is untouched

presets.name: Mono the lows
presets.desc: A stereo synth or backing with everything below 180 Hz made mono, the rest untouched
presets.notes: The vinyl and live rule, on the side only: the dry mid never sees a filter

presets.name: Place left
presets.desc: A guitar lane widened and placed left of centre without touching its mono fold
presets.notes: Pair with Place right on the other guitarist: different variants keep the two images distinct

presets.name: Place right
presets.desc: A guitar lane widened and placed right of centre without touching its mono fold
presets.notes: The partner of Place left: variant 3 against its 2

presets.name: Turn the keys
presets.desc: A stereo keyboard image rotated off-centre to the right, its spread kept
presets.notes: A true rotation of a stereo source; it moves the fold (stated), use Balance for a mono lane

presets.name: Width swell
presets.desc: Stereo opening with the expression pedal, from mono to fully decorrelated
presets.notes: Map EXP to Amount 0 - 100 %: the fold stays the dry at every position, no zipper

mode.name: Mode
mode.help: What drives the duck: the key's level, the key's onsets, or the beat

thresh.name: Threshold
thresh.help: Peak level of the filtered key where ducking starts

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: Full duck, a positive amount in dB, whatever the key's level above threshold + knee

attack.name: Attack
attack.help: Time to reach full depth (raised-cosine edge)

hold.name: Hold
hold.help: Stays ducked this long after the key drops: bridges the gaps between words

release.name: Release
release.help: Return from full depth to 0 dB

lpf.name: Key High Cut
lpf.help: Butterworth low-pass on the key (range widened from 500 Hz when coded: the kick settings use 150 Hz)

knee.name: Knee
knee.help: Key range over which the duck grows from 0 to depth

freq.name: Band Frequency
freq.help: Bell centre; Low / High: where half the duck applies

spread.name: Spectral Spread
spread.help: Spectral: how far below the key's loudest band a band still ducks

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Trigger: the dip's length as a note value

length.name: Dip Length
length.help: Share of the note value the dip lasts (sync on)

tension.name: Recovery Tension
tension.help: Recovery shape: + returns late (club pump), − snaps back

offset.name: Beat Offset
offset.help: Pump: shifts the dip within the period to sit on the kick

sens.name: Trigger Sensitivity
sens.help: Trigger: the rise an onset needs, 12 → 3 dB (gfx-swell's detector A; same direction as gfx-killswitch)

lookahead.name: Lookahead
lookahead.help: Delays the main, reported to the host

force.name: Duck Now
force.help: Momentary footswitch: ducks fully while held (talkback, breakdown)

presets.name: Pad under the voice
presets.desc: Lowers an ambient guitar pad by 9 dB while the singer sings, holding through the gaps between words
presets.notes: Key = the voice lane's DI. The key filters keep breath and stage rumble out; set thresh just above the mic's bleed at soundcheck

presets.name: Voice band carve
presets.desc: Cuts 8 dB from a pad only in a two-octave band around 1.5 kHz while the voice sings; the body stays
presets.notes: The pad keeps its loudness and lows; only the band the voice needs moves out of the way

presets.name: Spectral vocal space
presets.desc: Ducks a keys or synth bed by 8 dB only in the half-octave bands where the voice is loudest, moment by moment
presets.notes: 16 bells from 57 Hz to 10 kHz; spread 12 dB ducks the voice's formant regions and leaves the rest of the bed alone

presets.name: Solo spotlight
presets.desc: Makes room in the centre of a stereo backing for a band mate's solo, in its own bands; the width stays
presets.notes: Key = the soloist's lane output (needs golem's key_from). Mid only: the backing's side signal is untouched

presets.name: Talkover, mids
presets.desc: Pulls the music's midrange down 18 dB while the talk mic is used; bass and air stay up
presets.notes: Hold 600 ms bridges the pauses of speech; the 3-octave bell is the band of a speaking voice

presets.name: Talkover, full band
presets.desc: Lowers the whole music by 18 dB while the talk mic is used, back up a second after the last word
presets.notes: The broadcast talkover: a fixed depth whatever the level of the voice

presets.name: Talkback button
presets.desc: A footswitch that drops the signal by 18 dB while held, for talking to the band or the room
presets.notes: Duck Now on a momentary footswitch does the work; thresh 0 dB keeps any key from ducking. Never stored with Duck Now on

presets.name: Delay tail out of the way
presets.desc: On a wet-only branch: the repeats drop 12 dB while you play and swell back in the gaps
presets.notes: Works today: golem keys the block with the lane's DI. Knee 6 dB gives gfx-delay's own ducking curve, for effects without one

presets.name: Reverb tail out of the way
presets.desc: On a wet-only reverb branch: the wash sinks 10 dB under the playing and blooms when you stop
presets.notes: A slower return than the delay preset: the bloom rises over 600 ms instead of jumping back

presets.name: Kick ducks the sub
presets.desc: Each kick fires the same short 12 dB dip on the bass's lows only; the growl above 240 Hz stays
presets.notes: Key = the kick (needs golem's key_from). Level-independent dips; for a kick mic with bass bleed use hpf 2000 on the beater's click

presets.name: Kick ducks the sub, in time
presets.desc: Each kick dips the bass's lows 12 dB for 70 % of an eighth note, the recovery locked to the tempo
presets.notes: The recovery follows the song's tempo, so it never needs retuning between songs

presets.name: Club pump
presets.desc: The sidechain pump on every beat without a kick: a fast 18 dB dip that swells back late
presets.notes: Phase from the host's position: the dip lands on the beat. Positive tension keeps the gain low and returns it late

presets.name: Low-only pump
presets.desc: Pumps only the lows of a pad or clean chords on each beat, 24 dB deep; the top stays bright
presets.notes: A band split without a crossover: the shelf is out of the path between dips, so the top is never touched

presets.name: Half-time breathing
presets.desc: A gentle 6 dB dip every half note that snaps back early: the pad breathes with the groove
presets.notes: Negative tension returns the gain early and lands softly on 0 dB

presets.name: Clean deep duck, lookahead
presets.desc: Ducks 15 dB with a 5 ms fall that completes as the key's onset arrives: no tick on low sustained notes
presets.notes: 5 ms of reported latency: a studio or setup choice, not for live monitoring through the block

fuzz.name: Fuzz
fuzz.help: The model's fuzz / sustain / attack pot, on its own taper (face: 1 kΩ linear; muff: 100 kΩ)

tone.name: Tone
tone.help: Si Four: the stack's pot (0 = noon, the stock setting)

level.name: Level
level.help: 0 dB = unity loudness on every model; a gain after the circuit

guitar_vol.name: Guitar Vol
guitar_vol.help: The guitar's volume knob, real taper and impedance: the cleanup

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.help: A buffer between guitar and fuzz: low source impedance, no cleanup magic

pickup.name: Pickup
pickup.help: The guitar the DI was recorded with: coil, pots, cable

bias.name: Bias
bias.help: The trimmer: 0 = 4.5 V at 25 °C, 9 V; +100 % halves the resistor (bias_v up), −100 % doubles it (bias_v down)

temp.name: Temperature
temp.help: Device temperature: germanium drifts, silicon barely

leakage.name: Leakage
leakage.help: Germanium collector-junction leakage, relative: 100 % = the model's devices (inert on Si Pair, Si Four)

voltage.name: Voltage
voltage.help: Battery voltage: low = gated, sputtery; 18 V = more headroom

sag.name: Sag
sag.help: Battery internal resistance, 0 – 2 kΩ with a 47 µF reservoir

mids.name: Mids
mids.help: Si Four: fills the scoop (0 = stock)

input.name: Input
input.help: For a DI hotter or weaker than 0 dBFS = 1 V

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Linear crossfade dry ↔ fuzz, dry phase-aligned

presets.name: Sixties germanium
presets.desc: The germanium face at full fuzz, single coil loading its input: warm, round, not fizzy

refs.why: germanium two-transistor fuzz into a clean-ish stack

presets.notes: The reference face: the pickup's coil and pots in front of Q1 take the top off before anything clips

presets.name: Volume-knob clean
presets.desc: Full fuzz; roll the guitar volume (EXP) to 30 % for a bright, nearly clean tone at the same level
presets.notes: Measured: THD −7 dB at 100 %, −17 at 50 %, −23 at 30 % with the level within 2.5 dB; put EXP on guitar_vol

presets.name: Behind a buffer
presets.desc: The same face after a buffer: the volume knob only turns it down, the fuzz stays
presets.notes: To hear why a face wants to be first: buffered, the THD is 5 – 13 dB higher at every knob position

presets.name: Summer stage
presets.desc: Hot germanium at 35 °C: the face drifts off bias, thinner and splattier
presets.notes: Q2's collector moves 4.5 → 6.7 V (bias_v): less swing towards the supply

presets.name: Winter garage
presets.desc: Cold germanium at 12 °C: the face sinks towards saturation, darker and more compressed
presets.notes: bias_v about 3 V: Q2 nearer saturation

presets.name: Leaky pair
presets.desc: An unselected germanium pair (250 % leakage): biased high, thin and spitty
presets.notes: The pedal a builder would have rejected: Q2 sits near 6.5 V

presets.name: Misbiased spitter
presets.desc: The trimmer turned down (bias −70 %): Q2 near saturation, sputter on the decay
presets.notes: bias_v ≈ 1 V; which side gates best is for the ear (README §2.6)

presets.name: Starved gate
presets.desc: A dying 4 V battery with sag on the germanium face: notes chop off as they decay
presets.notes: The README's velcro gate is a silicon face (not shipped yet); on germanium the bias follows the supply: splattier than gated

presets.name: Dying battery
presets.desc: Put EXP on voltage and sweep 9 → 3 V: from full fuzz to a broken, sputtering gate

presets.name: Parallel fuzz
presets.desc: Germanium face blended 50 / 50 with the dry guitar: fuzz on top, the attack kept

presets.name: Swell fuzz
presets.desc: Put EXP on fuzz: the face's own pot swept under the foot, from boost-like to full fuzz

presets.name: Wall of sustain
presets.desc: Four-transistor muff, classic stack at noon: endless sustain with the mid scoop

refs.why: muff-type fuzz walls on 90s alternative records

presets.name: Doom wall
presets.desc: Russian stack, sustain high, tone towards the bass, a little mids: dark and thick

presets.name: Band-mix muff
presets.desc: Muff with the scoop filled (mids 80 %): stays audible in a band mix
presets.notes: 22 kΩ-class resistor in series with the low-pass cap: the notch shrinks and moves down

presets.name: Tone-bypassed muff
presets.desc: The muff with its tone stack removed: loud, flat and mid-heavy

presets.name: Eighteen-volt muff
presets.desc: The muff on an 18 V supply: more headroom, louder and less compressed

presets.name: Triangle lead
presets.desc: Early-1970s triangle-era stack, sustain 80 %, tone a touch bright: a singing lead

presets.name: Fuzz bass
presets.desc: Russian muff for bass: below 120 Hz the dry stays, a 70 % blend keeps the fundamental

fuzz.name: Fuzz
fuzz.help: The 1 kΩ B fuzz rheostat in the loop's AC ground (100 % = R_MIN): the series-series feedback around Q1 – Q3

octave.name: Octave
octave.help: Linear crossfade from the fuzz alone (0 %, the tap a · v(winding)) to the rectified output (100 %, the stock pedal); 50 % is a clone's lifted diode to first…

tone.name: Tone
tone.help: Tilt ±6 dB around 800 Hz after the circuit, 0 = off (the circuit has no tone control)

level.name: Level
level.help: 0 dB = unity loudness at the defaults (K = −21.7 dB; the volume pot fully up is level +21.7 dB)

guitar_vol.name: Guitar Vol
guitar_vol.help: The guitar's volume knob, real taper and impedance, in the netlist

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.help: A buffer between the guitar and the pedal: the pickup no longer sees the ≈ 270 kΩ input

pickup.name: Pickup
pickup.help: The guitar the DI was recorded with: coil, pots, cable

bias.name: Bias
bias.help: The trimmer R2 (Q1's base resistor, stock 680 kΩ) × 2^(+bias / 100): + raises bias_v (4.0 – 6.3 V at 9 V)

temp.name: Temperature
temp.help: Device temperature: the silicon barely moves, the germanium rectifier diodes follow

voltage.name: Voltage
voltage.help: Battery voltage: low = starved, 18 V = headroom

sag.name: Sag
sag.help: Battery internal resistance, 0 – 2 kΩ with a 47 µF reservoir

input.name: Input
input.help: For a DI hotter or weaker than 0 dBFS = 1 V

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Linear crossfade dry ↔ wet, the dry through the same oversampler path

presets.name: Octave ring
presets.desc: Neck humbucker, tone rolled back: the rectified octave rings over sustained notes above the 12th fret

refs.why: transformer octave fuzz on the neck pickup, high on the neck

presets.notes: Play single notes above the 12th fret and let them ring: 2f up to 24 dB over f on a held note at L_m = 1 H

presets.name: Octave bloom
presets.desc: The pick attack in fuzz, the octave growing as the note decays and the input clamp lets go
presets.notes: Hold single notes: the coupling capacitors release the bias over a few tens of ms and the octave swells in

presets.name: Octave blend
presets.desc: Half fuzz, half octave: the octave as a colour on a plain fuzz, chords stay readable
presets.notes: octave 50 % is a clone's lifted-diode position to first order: one half-wave added to the fuzz

presets.name: Ring chords
presets.desc: Full fuzz on double stops and bends: ring-modulator intermodulation and dive-bombs
presets.notes: The rectifier multiplies the notes of a double stop: sum and difference tones, the dive on a bent double stop

presets.name: Octave lead, hot
presets.desc: Raised bias and a 12 V supply: Q3 further from saturation, the octave holds on harder picking
presets.notes: bias_v ≈ 7.5 V at 12 V (4.9 V stock at 9 V): more headroom before the duty moves; to be judged by ear

bypass.name: Bypass

transpose.name: Transpose

string_2.help: Custom tuning's open string 2 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

string_3.name: String 3
string_3.help: Custom tuning's open string 3 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

string_4.name: String 4
string_4.help: Custom tuning's open string 4 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

string_5.name: String 5
string_5.help: Custom tuning's open string 5 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

string_6.name: String 6
string_6.help: Custom tuning's open string 6 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

string_7.name: String 7
string_7.help: Custom tuning's open string 7 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

string_8.name: String 8
string_8.help: Custom tuning's open string 8 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

threshold.name: Threshold
threshold.help: Level below which nothing is read (noisy rigs, hum)

always_on.name: Always On
always_on.help: Keep measuring while bypassed: drift badge during a song (PolyTune's "Display Always On")

presets.name: Stage silent
presets.desc: Mutes the output while engaged and names each plucked string in tens of ms against the lane's tuning
presets.notes: The pedal tuner between songs. golem sends the lane's tuning (Custom + strings) at insert; Fast settles in 0.2 – 0.8 s

presets.name: Stage silent, bass
presets.desc: Mutes the output while engaged and reads each bass string, the low B included, against the lane's tuning
presets.notes: Low strings take longer: the coarse note in 80 ms, the strobe reading from 0.45 s on a low B

presets.name: Strum check
presets.desc: Strum all the open strings at once: one column per string, the strings that share a partial dimmed
presets.notes: Neck pickup and a thumb strum keep the upper partials low; pluck a dimmed string alone to read it exactly

presets.name: Strobe setup
presets.desc: Chromatic strobe at ±0.1 ¢ with an honest settled flag, heard while tuning: intonation at the bench
presets.notes: Compare the open string with the 12th fret fretted, not the harmonic (sharp by the string's inharmonicity)

presets.name: Five-string low B
presets.desc: Reads a 5-string bass from its low B: long window down to 25 Hz, the strings prior against octave errors
presets.notes: Fast settles a clean low B in about 0.75 s; switch to Strobe for a final check (1 s, 2 s on a hard pluck)

presets.name: Drop A seven
presets.desc: Seven-string drop A (A1 E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4): the low A on the long window, each pluck on its string
presets.notes: A1 is 55 Hz: the long YIN window answers in about 80 ms

presets.name: Eight-string standard
presets.desc: Eight-string standard from the low F#: strings attributed by the tuning, strum read per string
presets.notes: On a strum the 8-string needs 0.85 s for its low strings: their neighbours are close in hertz

presets.name: Capo on 2
presets.desc: Standard tuning with every target two semitones up, for a capo on the 2nd fret
presets.notes: transpose shifts the string targets, not the reference

presets.name: Half step down
presets.desc: Every string a semitone down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb), each pluck attributed to its string
presets.notes: Same targets as 6-std with transpose −1; golem names them with flats

presets.name: Harmonic tuning
presets.desc: Tune with 12th-fret harmonics: each one is attributed to its own string, its offset included
presets.notes: A harmonic reads about 0.5 ¢ sharp of the open string's fundamental (inharmonicity); not corrected
